rows.headline: Libra New Moon
rows.body:
The Libra New Moon offers a beginning in how we meet one another. We may want to be understood while making ourselves so easy to agree with that our preferences barely enter the conversation. You say that anything is fine, then feel disappointed when the plan includes very little of what you wanted. The other person may have no idea what they are missing. With the Sun and Moon meeting in Libra, connection has a chance to grow around a more honest exchange.

Libra season teaches the difference between honest compromise and self-abandonment. We are learning that being direct can be an act of care, especially when it gives a relationship information it needs to grow. You may have been searching for words that guarantee a comfortable response. There is no magic script, but there can be a conversation in which both people are allowed to want something. Understanding another person’s perspective does not oblige you to surrender your own.

Venus, Libra’s ruler, draws us toward connection through what we find beautiful and worth sharing. In Libra, that attraction develops through getting to know another person and discovering how your lives might fit together. Shared pleasure matters. So does learning how each of you responds when your preferences differ. An agreement has more to offer when it reflects what both people value, including the differences that made you interested in each other in the first place.

In Greek mythology, Harmonia is the daughter of Aphrodite and Ares, the deities associated with Venus and Mars. Her parentage gives us an image of harmony born from the meeting of connection and assertion. Through Libra, we can understand agreement as something strengthened by each person’s ability to speak and choose. Your yes means more when you are free to refuse. The relationship gains something when you can participate willingly and take responsibility for what you offer.

The challenge is to remain honest about the relationship that is available. You may be so invested in what a connection could become that you overlook what the other person has said they can give. Their potential cannot make a commitment on their behalf. Let yourself enjoy the possibility while paying attention to how you treat each other now. Mutuality develops through the choices both people make, including their willingness to follow through when something needs to change.

Let your New Moon intentions describe the kind of connection you want to help create. Begin by giving your preferences a place in the conversation before an agreement is made. You will not get it right every time, and returning to clarify something can be part of learning how to care for each other. Repair is progress. Notice the pleasure of being met by someone who is glad you told them. Honesty can give a relationship more to grow from.

rows.headline: Pisces New Moon
rows.body:
The Pisces New Moon offers a beginning for the hopes we have been afraid to take seriously. We may have become so practiced at anticipating disappointment that we dismiss a possibility before it has the chance to move us. You sense that you want something different, then immediately require yourself to explain exactly how it would work. Some desires need time to become recognizable. With the Sun and Moon meeting in Pisces, imagination can help you discover what you are ready to nurture next.

Pisces season brings us to the end of the zodiac’s cycle, where an ending can change what we want from a beginning. You may be grieving a future that did not happen while discovering that another part of your life wants to grow. Both experiences deserve your attention. The meaning of an old dream can remain with you as its form changes. You are allowed to learn more about what you want without treating every revision as a failure to believe in yourself.

Jupiter, Pisces’s traditional ruler, connects this New Moon with faith and the search for meaning beyond what we already know. In this water sign, understanding can develop through what moves us before we can explain it. A creative or spiritual practice may help you recognize a feeling you have struggled to put into words. Give that experience time to affect your choices. Inspiration becomes part of your life through the attention you offer it and what you discover when you return.

In one telling of the story associated with Pisces, fish carry Aphrodite and Eros to safety as they flee Typhon. Help comes from the creatures of the water. The story offers an image of being supported when individual effort is no longer enough. Through Pisces, we can consider the receptivity involved in accepting that help. You may be so occupied with finding your own way forward that you overlook what someone is willing to offer. A beginning can include allowing yourself to receive.

The challenge is to remain in contact with what is happening while giving hope somewhere to grow. A strong feeling deserves attention, but it does not tell you everything about a situation. You may need to clarify what another person wants before making their participation part of a future you are imagining. Let new information affect the dream. An intention can guide your choices while leaving other people free to make their own, and your future free to develop beyond the first version you pictured.

Let your New Moon intention give inspiration a place in your days. Return to something that helps you feel connected to your own imagination, even while its purpose is still becoming clear. What develops may surprise you. You can support a dream through small acts of attention without deciding its final shape in advance. The experience can help you recognize which possibilities you want to develop and what they need from you. Allow the dream to become clearer through your relationship with it.

rows.headline: Sagittarius New Moon
rows.body:
The Sagittarius New Moon returns us to the pleasure of having something to look forward to. We may feel drawn toward a subject or experience, then dismiss the interest because we cannot explain where it will lead. You are already trying to justify the outcome of something you have barely begun to explore. With the Sun and Moon meeting in Sagittarius, curiosity can become a reason to begin. What you learn may change your sense of what is possible before it gives you a clear destination.

Sagittarius season teaches us to examine the beliefs through which we understand our lives. An explanation that once helped you may have become too limited for what you are encountering now. You may discover that you have been defending an idea because changing your mind would require reconsidering other choices. Give yourself permission to learn something that has consequences for what you believe. Growth includes being able to recognize when experience has taught you more than an old certainty can contain.

Jupiter, Sagittarius’s ruler, connects this New Moon with the search for meaning and the confidence to reach beyond familiar experience. A possibility becomes easier to imagine when you encounter someone who has pursued it. Their example can help you see a direction you had not considered, while their experience reveals what the pursuit involves. Let inspiration make you more interested in learning. You can believe that life has more to offer while becoming specific about what you want to explore.

Chiron, the wise centaur of Greek myth, teaches Asclepius the healing arts. His role as a teacher offers an image of possibility developed through a relationship with knowledge. Read through Sagittarius, the story connects the desire to grow with the willingness to be taught. Being drawn toward a field does not mean you should already know how to work within it. A good beginning can involve finding guidance that develops your judgment and gives your questions somewhere to go.

The challenge is to give an expansive vision enough attention to become an experience. Imagining the future can feel more exciting than the first ordinary task it requires. You may love the idea of knowing a subject and discover that learning it involves considerable patience. Let that discovery inform your approach. Enthusiasm can bring you to the beginning, while your willingness to return gives understanding a chance to develop. You can keep the larger aim without expecting every step to feel extraordinary.

Let your New Moon intention open a path toward something you want to understand or experience. Begin the preparation that would help you participate, and remain interested in what changes as you learn. Your first idea does not have to contain your entire future. The opportunity includes discovering a direction you could not have chosen with the knowledge you had before you began. Give yourself something to look forward to that also gives you something worth doing now.

rows.headline: Scorpio New Moon
rows.body:
The Scorpio New Moon brings us into contact with what we want to share and what we still keep protected. We may speak openly about difficult things that happened years ago while avoiding a simple admission about what we need now. You have told someone your history, but they may still have no idea how much the connection matters to you. A deeper beginning can involve letting yourself be known in the present, where another person’s response has the power to affect you.

Scorpio season teaches us to recognize the ways we protect ourselves and what those protections have begun to cost. A defense that once helped you may now limit an experience you want to have. You can respect the reason it developed while considering how much influence it needs today. Trust does not require giving everyone access to you. It develops as you learn who can respond to your honesty with care and whose actions support what they say.

With the Sun and Moon meeting in Scorpio, a new cycle begins in a sign traditionally ruled by Mars. Here, Mars’s power to protect and act becomes a capacity for sustained commitment. You decide what deserves your energy and what you are prepared to defend. A clear boundary can make closeness more possible because you understand what you are agreeing to. You can take a meaningful emotional risk while keeping a say in the pace and depth of the exchange.

In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, Hecate hears Persephone’s cry but does not see who took her. She tells Demeter what she knows and accompanies her in the search. Later, she becomes Persephone’s companion. Her role offers a way to think about trust through Scorpio: support includes being honest about what we do not know. Hecate’s willingness to help does not depend on having the whole explanation. Her presence gives Demeter someone with whom to continue the search.

The challenge is to recognize when a test has replaced a conversation. You may keep an important need hidden, then take someone’s failure to notice as evidence that they do not care. That leaves both of you responding to an arrangement only one person understands. You can choose what remains private while being clear about what affects a shared decision. Trust has more opportunity to grow when someone has enough information to respond and you allow their response to inform what happens next.

Let your New Moon intention begin with a degree of openness you are willing to practice. Choose someone whose actions have earned that access, and let them know something that matters now. You do not have to tell your whole story at once. Pay attention to how the exchange feels and what follows it. A different experience becomes possible when the person in front of you has a chance to show you who they are, and you have a chance to decide what you want to build together.

You can respect the reason it developed while considering how much influence it needs today. Trust does not require giving everyone access to you. It develops as you learn who can respond to your honesty with care and whose actions support what they say.

With the Sun and Moon meeting in Scorpio, a new cycle begins in a sign traditionally ruled by Mars. Here, Mars’s power to protect and act becomes a capacity for sustained commitment. You decide what deserves your energy and what you are prepared to defend. A clear boundary can make closeness more possible because you understand what you are agreeing to. You can take a meaningful emotional risk while keeping a say in the pace and depth of the exchange.

In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, Hecate hears Persephone’s cry but does not see who took her. She tells Demeter what she knows and accompanies her in the search. Later, she becomes Persephone’s companion. Her role offers a way to think about trust through Scorpio: support includes being honest about what we do not know. Hecate’s willingness to help does not depend on having the whole explanation. Her presence gives Demeter someone with whom to continue the search.

The challenge is to recognize when a test has replaced a conversation. You may keep an important need hidden, then take someone’s failure to notice as evidence that they do not care. That leaves both of you responding to an arrangement only one person understands. You can choose what remains private while being clear about what affects a shared decision. Trust has more opportunity to grow when someone has enough information to respond and you allow their response to inform what happens next.

Let your New Moon intention begin with a degree of openness you are willing to practice. Choose someone whose actions have earned that access, and let them know something that matters now. You do not have to tell your whole story at once. Pay attention to how the exchange feels and what follows it. A different experience becomes possible when the person in front of you has a chance to show you who they are, and you have a chance to decide what you want to build together.

rows.headline: Taurus New Moon
rows.body:
The Taurus New Moon is an opportunity to stop postponing the life we are working to create. We may tell ourselves that once the next project is finished, we will finally slow down and enjoy what we have earned. Then the project ends, another takes its place, and the time we promised ourselves disappears again. You can keep improving your circumstances and still feel as though your life is waiting on the other side of more work. What is all that effort supposed to give you?

Taurus season teaches us to build a relationship with enough. You can want greater stability and still let yourself enjoy your life along the way. With the Sun and Moon meeting in Taurus, consider what abundance would allow you to experience. More time to yourself may matter as much as more money. Let your intentions reflect what you value, including the pleasure of living in a body that receives care. What you are building needs to sustain the person who is building it.

Venus, Taurus’s ruler, connects this New Moon with our capacity to appreciate and receive pleasure. In this earth sign, what we value takes shape through what we cultivate over time. You may say that having time to yourself matters, then repeatedly offer it away before considering what you wanted to do with it. Your preferences need some influence over your decisions if they are going to become part of your experience. Enjoyment deserves a place in the arrangement from the beginning.

In the story of King Midas, his wish to turn everything he touches into gold becomes unbearable when even his food is transformed. He receives exactly what he requested and discovers that he cannot live on it. The story gives Taurus a question worth considering: what do you want your abundance to make possible? The answer may change what you are willing to spend your time acquiring. Something can be valuable and still cost more of your life than you want to give it.

The challenge is to recognize when the pursuit of stability has become a reason to keep everything as it is. You may continue maintaining something because you have already invested so much in it, even as it gives you less in return. Familiarity can make that arrangement easier to defend than to reconsider. Take an honest look at what it requires now and what you receive from continuing. You are allowed to update your priorities as you learn more about what satisfies you.

Let your New Moon intention name something you want to experience, then give it a place in your ordinary life. If you want more time to enjoy what you have built, consider which commitment you could stop renewing automatically. A desire becomes easier to support when you understand what it needs from you. You do not have to finish earning your future before you can participate in your present.

rows.headline: Virgo New Moon
rows.body:
You do not need another plan for becoming a better version of yourself. You may need to stop treating every difficult part of your life as evidence that you need fixing. The Virgo New Moon brings our attention to the systems holding ordinary life together and the effort they require. This is where we notice what has become difficult to maintain and what only works because we keep compensating for it.

Virgo season teaches us that care takes shape through what we do repeatedly. A good intention needs a way to survive an ordinary day, including the days when your energy changes or something takes longer than expected. With the Sun and Moon meeting in Virgo, consider what would help the life you have run more smoothly. You may have built a routine around a version of yourself who never needs extra time. That is useful information about the routine.

Virgo is ruled by Mercury, but its intelligence is practical. It notices what is useful, what is wasting your time, and what could work better with a small adjustment. Here, discernment helps you understand the difference between effort that serves a purpose and effort you have become accustomed to making. Sometimes progress is realizing that the routine you keep failing at was never built for the life you actually have.

In Greek myth, Ariadne gives Theseus a thread that allows him to find his way out of the labyrinth. Entering is only part of the problem; he also needs a way to return. Her contribution offers an image of the foresight that makes a difficult undertaking possible. Through Virgo, we can recognize the value of a method that remains useful when our attention is strained. You do not have to solve the same problem from the beginning every time it returns.

The challenge is recognizing when improvement has become another way to criticize yourself. You can keep refining the plan and raising the standard until nothing you do feels finished. Perfectionism can look like discipline and responsibility while quietly making you dissatisfied with everything you accomplish. Before making another adjustment, consider what it would actually improve. Some work is ready to be used, shared, or left alone long before you run out of things you could change.

Let your New Moon intention make care more practical. Choose something that would help your days work better for the person you are now, then pay attention to the difference it makes. You can revise the approach as you learn what helps. The coming months do not need a flawless plan. They need a life that does not require you to keep treating yourself as the problem.

rows.headline: Aquarius
rows.summary: What truth have I been hiding because I thought it was too much, too different, too revolutionary?
rows.body: If you've been playing by rules that were never yours, following paths that made sense to everyone except you, this New Moon in Aquarius is your permission slip to stop fitting in where you were never meant to belong. If you've spent so long making yourself smaller to be understood, editing your truth to be palatable, it's time to stop. What if your weirdness is exactly what the world needs? What if the thing that makes you different is the thing that makes you valuable? Stop apologizing for seeing things differently. Your revolution doesn't need anyone's approval.

If you've been so busy nurturing everyone else that you forgot you deserve care too, this is your reminder. Your needs aren't an inconvenience. They're valid.

sections.intention: What would I build if I actually believed I was worth it?
sections.ritual: Plant something in soil: seeds, a plant, or even place your hands on the earth. Set an intention for what you want to grow slowly and sustainably in terms of worth and value.

packageRecord.body: If you've been undervaluing yourself for so long that it feels normal, accepting less because you didn't want to seem difficult, giving discounts on your worth because someone made you feel like you were asking for too much, this New Moon in Taurus is here to remind you that your worth isn't negotiable. It's not up for debate. You don't have to earn it through endless giving or prove it through exhaustion. Your value exists whether anyone sees it or not. Stop apologizing for having standards. Stop shrinking to make others comfortable with your abundance.

rows.headline: Virgo
rows.summary: What would my daily life look like if it was built from self-love instead of self-improvement?
rows.body: If you've been using perfectionism as armor, thinking if you could just get it right, be good enough, organized enough, disciplined enough, then you'd finally feel worthy, this New Moon in Virgo is calling you out. Your worth doesn't come from your productivity. Your value isn't measured in how perfectly you can perform wellness. This is about creating routines that actually nourish you, not ones that look good on social media. Stop punishing yourself with self-improvement. Start caring for yourself with compassion.

Give the idea a calendar, a budget, or a first visible step before expecting it to carry more.

rows.headline: Venus stations direct

A conversation may resume, an old connection may look different once the nostalgia wears off, or a financial choice may become easier to judge with the full cost in view. Do not expect every answer tonight. The next few weeks may show what still belongs in your life, what needs different expectations, and what only looked appealing while the past was close.

rows.headline: Venus stations retrograde
rows.body: Venus turns retrograde today, beginning several weeks of review around relationships, money, creative work, appearance, and what you still want. An ex, former friend, old project, unpaid expense, or purchase you regret may return because the decision was never fully settled. Nostalgia usually presents the best evidence first, so wait before making a permanent relationship decision, major purchase, investment, tattoo, haircut, or dramatic change in how you present yourself. The question is not simply if you can have it again. It is if it still fits the person and life you have now.

rows.headline: If it still stings, it isn't finished.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, this transit {{aspectWord}} your Chiron. Everyday events can set off an old hurt or insecurity. A passing comment or being left out of a plan can hurt as much as every earlier time it happened. That sting makes sense. You end up answering what someone said years ago instead of what this person said today, and a small issue turns into a big argument. When a remark stings, answer only what was said today.

You may notice the urge to protect the sore spot before deciding if the person in front of you is actually repeating the old pattern. The two concerns sit close together now, so the issue moving from background to action immediately changes how you experience the situation instead of arriving as a separate issue.

rows.headline: What you've been avoiding is the missing piece.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, this transit {{aspectWord}} your nodal axis. You feel pulled between what you do well and a direction you have barely started. The familiar skill feels safe. The new one makes you feel clumsy and exposed. An offer or a deadline can force you to pick. Each time you go back to the comfortable option, you skip the practice the new direction needs, and the new skill stays clumsy longer.

Their first tries at the new thing are rough, and they hate looking like a beginner in front of people who know them as the capable one.

rows.headline: You see what you never got, and what it taught you.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Chiron. For many months, sometimes more than a year, you see your oldest hurts with more distance than before. This comes once in a life, usually between your late thirties and around fifty. What you never got, from a parent, a teacher, a partner, or a job, becomes clear, and it can make you sad or angry. You can see what those years taught you, too. People with the same struggle start coming to you, and you know how to help them because you have lived it.

rows.headline: An old insecurity gets pressed, and you can handle it differently.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Chiron. For many months, an old hurt or insecurity gets pressed by what is happening now. This comes twice in a life, first in your teens or twenties and again in middle age. A rejection, a criticism, or a problem with your health can bring back the feeling that something is wrong with you. You doubt yourself, and you can react the way you did when the hurt was new, by hiding it or trying too hard. This time you can catch the old reaction as it starts and respond differently than you did before.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Jupiter. New opportunities arrive with an old feeling that you are not good enough. A bigger role or offer can look like your chance to finally prove someone wrong, and that makes it hard to see what the offer gives you. You could say yes to more work than you have time for, or turn down a good one because getting your hopes up feels risky. Both reactions come from the same old hurt. Before you commit, write down what the offer requires in hours and money. Anything you take on to prove a point is hard to quit once it stops being worth the cost.

packageRecord.body_you_alternate:
A moment of real growth can unexpectedly pull an old insecurity straight to the surface. When a big opportunity makes you second-guess yourself, the immediate reflex is to overcompensate. You might feel a sudden, intense pressure to say yes to everything and overcommit, just to prove you actually deserve the space you are taking up. The opportunity itself may be good. The problem starts when you turn it into proof that you can handle more, carry more, or ask less in return. You do not have to make an opportunity harder on yourself to feel like you earned it.

With Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Jupiter until {{untilDate}}, you can step fully into this expansion without letting insecurity push you into a massive obligation you will just have to back out of later.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. An old shame about wanting too much, or about being too angry or too direct, is easy to set off. A mild hint that you should be quieter or ask for less can hurt more than the person meant. Your first impulse is to apologize, even when what you wanted or how you reacted was reasonable. You learned to apologize a long time ago to stay safe. Each apology now repeats the old message that this part of you is a problem.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. Over this long stretch, the old shame about your anger or your wants hurts less, and you can look at where it came from. You feel tender toward the younger you who learned to hide those feelings to get by. You might tell someone about a time you were mocked for wanting more. When someone says you are too loud, you can keep talking, and each time you do, you believe the old message less. Because you know how that shame feels, you can help someone else who is being told they are too much.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Mars. Your anger comes faster, and it brings up old grudges. Being blocked or ignored can feel like the same insult you have taken before, so you push harder than the problem needs. Sometimes it goes the other way, and you hold the anger in until your shoulders ache and nothing gets done. Either way, your effort goes into proving nobody can dismiss you, and the problem that started it never gets solved.

The intensity comes from older moments when they could not stand up for themselves, so the reaction is bigger than the obstacle.

Your anger shows you what needs to change, and you can act on it without losing your temper. You could finally ask for the change you want, make a decision you have put off, or start exercising again after an injury or setback. If you wait until you feel calm about it, the drive may be gone by then.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Chiron {{aspectWord}} your Midheaven. An old fear of not being good enough, or of not being taken seriously, comes back around how you are seen and where you are headed. A low grade, a rejection from a job you applied for, or a relative's comment about how you run your household can feel like proof the fear was right. Being judged that way hurts. You could overwork to make up for it, or decide privately that you were never suited to the path you chose. Neither one fixes the problem in front of you, and both cost you sleep and the confidence you need to keep going.

A small slight from someone close can feel like proof that your needs never count, and being tired makes it worse. You could pick a fight with the nearest person or go silent and resentful. Both are ways of asking for care, and neither one gets it for you. Eat and sleep before you decide which disappointment to bring up.

Offers and encouragement are more likely to show up. With so much going well, you could split your time across several pleasant projects, or coast because nothing forces a choice. Pick one project you want to grow over these months and give it set hours each week.

An opening can make the whole situation look more promising to you, with confidence and the cost of expanding becoming the place where expansion is most tempting. A bigger purchase, broader plan, generous offer, or ambitious promise can look easier to support than it will feel later. You can use the impulse to expand before checking the cost while the timing is cooperative instead of waiting for urgency to create momentum.

The decision point in Jupiter {{aspectWord}} your Jupiter through {{untilDate}} is simple: you get more from one supported expansion than from three promises competing for the same money and schedule.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Jupiter {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. You have held back desire and anger for a long time, and you are less willing to keep doing it to keep the peace. An old arrangement could suddenly feel unbearable, or you could want something you were taught to be ashamed of. You have good reason to be angry. Your anger can help you say what you will no longer accept. It gets costly when you use it to punish people or to prove you were right.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Jupiter {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. Over these months, you are kinder to yourself about what you want. The parts of you that people once called too much feel less shameful, and the people around you are more accepting of the wants you used to hide. You could spend money on a pleasure you used to deny yourself, or tell someone that an arrangement no longer works for you. They are more likely to agree than you expected. Each time that goes well, asking for what you want gets easier. The same confidence can lead you to say yes to every want at once, and over a few months those choices cost money and time.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Jupiter {{aspectWord}} your Mars. Your drive is high and your patience is short. You want to push through work and arguments at full strength, and you feel capable of more than your body or schedule can take. That confidence can end in a strained muscle or an argument fought long past the point that mattered. Decide on a pace you could keep up for a month, and stop there each day.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Jupiter {{aspectWord}} your Midheaven. People are noticing what you do, and the people in charge are ready to back you. A teacher could recommend you for a program, a past contact could pass your name along while you job hunt, or a group could ask you to lead a project. These openings go to people whose results are known, so keeping your work to yourself costs you. Nobody can recommend you for a role they do not know you want. Tell the people who can help what you want next.

Someone close could offer an impressive opportunity, praise you heavily, or be so confident that your own goals start to look small. Some of it is generous and some of it serves them. You could claim you can do more than you can to keep up, or go along with their plan. Ask what the offer would need from you each week, and compare it with what you wanted before it came along.

sections.body_they: Through {{untilDate}}, Jupiter {{aspectWord}} their Sun. Someone else's ambition or approval is steering their choices right now. They could be getting big offers, a lot of praise, or advice from a confident person, and it is hard for them to tell how much of the plan is theirs. They might compete with that person instead of deciding for themselves. They could agree to a plan that impresses other people and later find it does not fit what they wanted.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Jupiter {{aspectWord}} your Sun. Confidence comes easily, and people respond well when you put yourself forward. Presenting your work, or asking for a raise, a grant, or a spot in a program, is likely to get support. The ease can make you coast and wait for recognition to find you. Share a piece of work you are proud of, under your own name.

rows.headline: Jupiter conjunction your Uranus
rows.body: With transiting Jupiter conjunct your natal Uranus through {{untilDate}}, unexpected opportunities shake up your usual schedule. You might feel a strong pull to drop boring habits, try a new routine, or pitch an unconventional project. Embrace these fresh options, but keep a notebook handy so you don't forget crucial details while moving fast. Trying a direct, alternative approach gets quick results.

sections.body_they: With transiting Jupiter conjunct their natal Uranus through {{untilDate}}, they bring an inventive spark into everything they tackle. Friends will notice them testing out unusual methods, changing their schedule on short notice, or starting fresh projects. They show how welcoming sudden updates unlocks surprising freedom.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Jupiter {{aspectWord}} your Uranus. Restlessness is growing, and you want freedom in a big way. Sudden urges to quit or move can feel thrilling, and surprises from outside could push in the same direction. Changing everything at once can solve the one problem that bothers you and break the routines and relationships that were working. Most of the urge is restlessness, and changing one part of your life may be enough to ease it.

rows.headline: Jupiter opposition your Uranus
rows.body: With transiting Jupiter opposite your natal Uranus through {{untilDate}}, sudden schedule changes or unexpected rule shifts can throw off your long-term plans. Jumping into unverified deals out of sheer boredom will backfire quickly. Keep a cool head, read contract fine print carefully, and enjoy the excitement without risking your daily stability.

rows.body: With transiting Jupiter square your natal Uranus through {{untilDate}}, impatience with rules can tempt you to make impulsive decisions or walk away from commitments prematurely. Rash financial bets or sharp outbursts will not give you the freedom you want. Give yourself room to blow off steam without breaking agreements that still work for you.

It is a good time to address hard topics directly, cut through long-standing complaints, and drop obligations you never agreed to carry. Speak your mind plainly without apologizing for holding your ground.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Mars {{aspectWord}} your Ascendant. You have more drive and less patience, and it shows in how you move and act before you say a word. You could talk faster, walk into rooms ready to push, or hear a neutral question as a challenge. People react to your intensity more than to your point, so conversations get tense. Rushing makes you clumsy, and you are more likely to hurt yourself. Get a workout in before a difficult conversation, and you will go into it calmer.

Rest the part of your body that hurts before you use it hard again.

rows.headline: Mars conjunction your Jupiter · cancer houses 6/6
rows.body:
You might feel an intoxicating rush of energy right now, one that tricks you into believing you have the boundless stamina to carry everyone else's burdens. Because this massive surge of optimism is flooding the sector of your chart that rules your daily grind, your first instinct is to play the hero and fix every problem in your orbit. But your physical energy is a finite resource. When you impulsively say yes to another favor, you are writing a check your nervous system will have to cash later.

Instead of scattering this beautiful momentum by playing caretaker to the crowd, pull that focus inward. Channel this fiery drive into aggressively clearing out your own backlog and building routines that actually nourish you.

With Mars {{aspectWord}} your Jupiter until {{untilDate}}, you do not have to prove your worth through endless acts of service. Let your optimism fuel you, but ruthlessly protect your boundaries. You can be profoundly generous without making burnout your baseline.

rows.body:
You may have less patience when someone assumes you’ll cover another expense, especially if you’ve already been stretching your budget to help. It might not be the amount that bothers you so much as the fact that nobody thought to ask. You want to be generous, but you also need enough for yourself.

With Mars {{aspectWord}} your Moon until {{untilDate}}, your protective instincts over your resources and energy are dialed all the way up. Let this surge of assertiveness work for you. If you've been letting things slide, this is your cosmic push to speak up.

Ask for what you’re owed. Be honest about what you can realistically contribute, and gently close the door on arrangements that no longer serve you. If you recently lost your temper, you can apologize for the delivery without taking back the boundary. Your limits are sacred.

If they tell you a plan is out of their budget, honor their "no" without trying to negotiate. They may sound a bit more forceful right now, especially if they’ve been overextending themselves or quietly covering costs to keep the peace.

With Mars {{aspectWord}} their Moon until {{untilDate}}, their internal anxieties around scarcity might manifest as irritation. If they seem unusually frustrated over a minor expense, remember it’s likely a buildup of feeling taken for granted. Instead of getting defensive, ask them what’s really on their mind.

Show them they are valued by being mindful of costs, asking before borrowing, and honoring your debts to them. If they snap, give the conversation a little breathing room before circling back. Their boundaries absolutely deserve your respect, and holding space for those limits creates a much healthier, balanced dynamic for you both.

rows.headline: Mercury conjunction your Jupiter
rows.body: With transiting Mercury conjunct your natal Jupiter through {{untilDate}}, your mind focuses on big-picture plans and positive solutions. It is a great time to learn something new or map out long-range goals. Just double-check your calendar and budget before taking on huge new promises so you do not overcommit.

An offer, or your own idea, can sound so good in conversation that you agree before anyone mentions cost, hours, or who does the work. You could claim to know more than you do, or promise to finish sooner than you can. Before you say yes or send the confident reply, write down the numbers and read them once.

Use that sharp focus to knock out annoying chores, dive into complicated paperwork, or power through a task list you've been putting off. Just double-check your tone before sending a quick text so you don't accidentally start a fight. Directing that energy into getting things done will clear out your mental clutter without creating unnecessary drama.

Trying to hide your vulnerability behind a tough exterior or over-functioning for others will only make your spirit feel more exhausted. Practice sitting directly with the physical discomfort without trying to fix it instantly or pretending you are fine when you are not.

They show how honoring their sore spots leads to genuine self-respect.

rows.headline: You're not hungry, you're bored.

Your feelings are bigger than what is going on, so you could eat more, spend more, or say yes to more than you planned, because doing something feels better than sitting still with the restlessness. rows.headline: Don't spend the win before it lands.

You could treat a raise, a refund, or a sale as settled before it is confirmed, and start spending the money or telling people about it. Your mood is making you this sure. Anything you pay for or promise now is owed in full if the result comes late or smaller. Celebrate once the money is in your account.

rows.headline: Moon opposition your Jupiter
rows.body: With the transiting Moon opposite your natal Jupiter through {{untilDate}}, a strong pull toward overindulgence, instant gratification, or escaping reality can clash directly with the steady demands of your ordinary routine. Ground yourself by consciously balancing your desire for comfort and expansion against what actually keeps your life stable, remembering that true ease comes from moderation rather than shortcuts. Keep your boundaries clear, protect your energy from burnout, and ensure you are not trading long-term peace for short-term distraction.

Observers will see them hold a steady center, make practical compromises, and keep their commitments balanced without unnecessary drama. They are actively working through the delicate art of honoring their expansive impulses while respecting real-world limits.

rows.headline: Moon square your Jupiter
rows.body: With the transiting Moon square your natal Jupiter through {{untilDate}}, a sudden urge to take on too much, overextend your energy, or say yes to things that drain your reserves can create unnecessary friction. Pull back your commitments, respect the very real limits of your physical and mental capacity, and avoid chasing tempting shortcuts that promise the world but leave you depleted. Protect your peace by practicing the art of saying no to over-enthusiastic obligations that sound wonderful in theory but cost too much in practice.

sections.body_they: With the transiting Moon square their natal Jupiter through {{untilDate}}, they navigate a brief temptation to overcommit, spend carelessly, or stretch their daily resources far too thin. Friends will watch them catch themselves, pull back on unrealistic plans, scale down their calendar, and refocus on what is genuinely and practically manageable today. They are doing the quiet work of reigning in grand pipe dreams in favor of sustainable, grounded choices.

rows.headline: Moon trine your Jupiter
rows.body: With the transiting Moon trine your natal Jupiter through {{untilDate}}, emotional ease and quiet optimism come together to make your day deeply restorative and sweet. You handle your home life, personal projects, and daily interactions with a warm, steady confidence, feeling fully supported by your own inner resilience and faith in the future. Let yourself completely rest, drop any unnecessary vigilance, and take in the natural goodwill and abundance surrounding you. You deserve moments where things simply work out and comfort finds you right where you are.

Friends and colleagues will notice them create a welcoming atmosphere, solve minor domestic snags with magnanimity, and enjoy a quiet, unforced happiness that brings comfort to all. They move through the day anchored in a deep, generative goodwill that makes everyone around them feel safe and valued.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the Moon {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. Irritation you usually keep to yourself comes out today. Ordinary requests feel like one more demand to be agreeable, and you want to refuse or make a cutting remark. That anger makes sense, because you have given in many times. Its size today comes from your mood as much as from the request. Turn down the one task you do not want to do. If you raise the bigger complaint about always being the agreeable one today, it will come out as an attack.

rows.headline: You're at ease with yourself today.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the Moon {{aspectWord}} your Mercury. Your thinking and your feelings agree today, so you feel sure of your own decisions. You can read a situation, form an opinion, and say it without second-guessing yourself. That helps with a task or project you have put off because you could not settle on an approach. Decide one open question and tell the people waiting on it. A decision made while your head and your mood agree is one you are less likely to reopen.

An email gets reread, a conversation changes direction halfway through, or a decision becomes harder once another person adds new information. The fact that changes the plan may arrive in a message, document, meeting, or correction that cannot be ignored once it is seen. There is less resistance between the body registering the situation quickly and what the situation needs, which gives you a better chance to use the opening deliberately. With your Mercury, the useful distinction is between what changed and the meaning the first reaction attached to it.

Talking about chores and plans at home goes more smoothly for about a day, because you can say what you need without it sounding like a complaint. Sorting out who does what, planning a meal or a visit, or explaining a change to family takes less going back and forth. You hear what others are asking for more accurately. Bring up the household subject that turns into an argument every time, and make your request in a sentence or two.

rows.headline: Handle the paperwork while your brain is quick.

Pick the joint task that keeps getting put off, like a budget or a schedule, and go through it together.

rows.headline: Done is the best status update.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the Moon {{aspectWord}} your Midheaven. Today you want your effort to be seen, and that is fair. Wanting credit can push you toward telling people about the work instead of finishing it. You could spend an hour talking about an assignment, an application, or a job around the house when the same hour would have finished it. Finish the task with a deadline before you tell anyone about it.

packageRecord.body_you_alternate:

A professional disagreement can become easier to handle once you separate the quality of the work from the politics around who gets recognized for it. What matters is the live consequence: an immediate emotional need becoming louder changes what you notice, needs, or chooses in the moment. Your Midheaven gives you a clearer clue once you compare the immediate reaction with what is still true an hour later.

rows.headline: Ask the person who's done it before.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the Moon {{aspectWord}} your Midheaven. For about a day, choices about where your life is going feel emotional and personal. Home and your role outside it both make demands on you, and a decision about one seems to say something about the other. You could spend hours thinking about going back to school, returning to paid work after caring for family, or changing what you do, trying to feel sure before you decide. A relative or friend who made a similar choice can tell you what it involved. Ask them one question about how it worked out for them instead of asking for reassurance.

rows.headline: Tired and hopeless feel identical at midnight.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the Moon {{aspectWord}} your Neptune. You tire sooner today, and your focus drifts. With a deadline coming, that tiredness can feel like proof that you are behind or that the work will never get done. Tired and discouraged feel alike from the inside, and today they are easy to mix up. Do the simplest part of the task, then stop for the night. Judged tonight, the work will look worse than it is.

At home you could forget chores halfway through, lose track of time, or picture changes to your home or family life in detail. The daydreaming is useful, because it shows you what you are wishing for. It turns into a problem when it becomes promises or purchases before you check the cost. Write down what you are picturing, and decide about any of it tomorrow.

The advantage is practical: mood changing the scale of the moment is easier to direct toward something useful instead of spending the day managing friction around it. Your Venus gives you a clearer clue once you compare the immediate reaction with what is still true an hour later.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Ascendant. For months, you are less sure how you come across. You may not know what kind of person you are showing people, and others can read you in ways you did not intend. You could find yourself turning into whatever each group seems to expect, because fitting in feels safer than being misread. Changing yourself for every group is tiring, and the more you do it, the less you know what you like. When you are unsure how you came across, ask a friend who knows you well instead of guessing.

You may find yourself telling someone you have just met about a dream you usually laugh off. This time, you do not rush to explain why it probably won’t happen. Something about the connection makes it easier to admit how much it matters. The sensitivity you have tried to conceal, the imagination you have dismissed as impractical, the longing for a more meaningful life can become reasons people are drawn to you. You do not have to make yourself less of any of these things to be understood.

With Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Ascendant until {{untilDate}}, take a step toward what has been quietly calling your attention. Show someone what you have been creating, accept an invitation that inspires you, or explore a spiritual interest you have kept private. An immediate connection still needs time to become trust, but that does not make it less worth exploring. Let someone inspire you without handing them the authority to tell you who you are.

A conversation that moves beyond the usual updates may reveal something surprising. They might admit they have started making art again or talk about an experience they are still trying to understand. Take an interest before deciding how well it fits the person they have always been. They may be discovering that something they once dismissed matters deeply to them, and a familiar joke about how unlike them this seems could make them wish they had said nothing.

With Neptune {{aspectWord}} their Ascendant until {{untilDate}}, an invitation can mean more than advice. Go with them to the exhibition, introduce them to someone who shares their interest, or listen to what they have been creating without immediately suggesting how to improve it. They do not need a finished plan to deserve encouragement. Let them share what moves them without having to defend why it matters.

rows.headline: Conjunction
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Chiron. An old hurt is easy to set off right now, and it can show up as sadness you cannot explain. Other people's pain hits you harder too. You could spend your evenings trying to rescue someone, or numb your feelings with shows and your phone. Both wear you out, and the old hurt stays where it was. If you write about it or talk to a therapist, you deal with the hurt instead of working around it.

rows.headline: Opposition

You could hope a partner or friend will make the old pain go away, or feel it is your job to fix theirs. When neither happens, you feel let down. One disappointing conversation can seem to prove an old fear before you know what happened. Ask them what they meant before you decide why they did it.

A book, a class, or one good conversation can show you a way to work on it. You understand other people's pain well, and you can help them with what you learned. These chances come without a deadline, so it is easy to let them go by. When one comes up, sign up that same day.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. Wants and resentment you have pushed down for a long time are harder to ignore. They come out as restlessness, daydreams, and guilt instead of wants you can name. You could fantasize about a person or a life you are not supposed to want, or feel resentful without knowing why. People who use guilt can get you to do what they want. If you act on the feeling before you can name it, you can end up in a commitment you did not choose. Write down what you want before you decide what to do about it.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Midheaven. Your direction feels unclear for a long stretch, and goals you used to care about can seem pointless. Promises from people in charge can sound bigger than they turn out to be, and it is hard to tell how others see you. A new job, a degree, or a business idea can look better than it is, and someone you looked up to may let you down. If you make a big move while you are this unsure, you can end up somewhere new with the same doubts. Get every offer and promise in writing before you leave what you have.

Some of it is not knowing what a responsibility will ask of them. They put off routine tasks and then feel further behind. The dread comes from not knowing what is due, and each skipped task makes it harder to find out.
packageRecord.body_you_alternate:
You may have less certainty and less energy at the same time, which makes limits and the work that can no longer be covered harder to read cleanly. The tedious task can become the thing blocking the interesting task until someone finally finishes it. The conflict gets clearer once you separate what actually changed from the extra pressure created by uncertainty mixing with sensitivity.

With Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Saturn until {{untilDate}}, you do better when you distinguish a meaningful limit from the pile of unfinished tasks making everything feel more restricted than it is.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Saturn. For months, you can turn an ideal into a routine you keep. Limits feel less harsh, and it is easier to stick with work you care about, like a creative project, a spiritual practice, or a slow plan to change your work. A clear rule or a firm no comes as a relief, because it tells you what you are working with. Because nothing feels pressing, the routine part is easy to put off. Set a weekly schedule for the project now, while you want to work on it.

A limit frustrates them less, because it shows them what is possible. With so little pressure, the work can stall without anyone noticing.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your South Node. For months, you are drawn back to familiar habits and old roles, most of all when the future feels unclear. You could miss how things used to be, go back to old ways of coping, or step back into a job people used to rely on you for. The old ways feel good because you already know how to do them. They cost you time and attention you meant to give a new direction. Before you say yes to an old role, decide how much of it you want.

sections.body_they: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} their South Node. For a long while, they keep going back to what is familiar. Old friends and old routines look comforting, partly because they cannot picture what comes next. People may ask them to step back into a job they used to do, and saying no is hard for them right now. Going back feels like rest to them. It also takes time they meant to spend on something new, and weeks can pass before they notice.

A vague plan, strong feeling, or missing detail can matter more than expected for you around the job everyone already expects you to do. Other people may quickly hand you the job you always know how to do, especially if that competence has made you the default helper before. The contact concentrates lower energy making certainty harder to force around one part of life, which can make a familiar pattern easier to recognize because it is harder to avoid.

While Neptune {{aspectWord}} your South Node until {{untilDate}}, you get more from deciding consciously where the old habit still serves you and where it simply saves other people from adjusting.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Sun. Your sense of who you are, and what you want to be known for, is blurry for months. You feel tired and less sure of yourself. Praise means little, or it seems meant for a version of you that no longer fits. You could hold on to a role or goal because it looks right to other people, while you lose interest in private. Pushing harder to feel sure of yourself only makes you more tired. The work you would do with no credit attached shows what you want now.

Their confidence comes back slowly, through work and interests they enjoy for their own sake.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Uranus. You feel restless and stuck for months, and the life you want instead is blurry. You could want to leave a routine, a job, or an arrangement in one dramatic move, mostly because not knowing is hard to bear. If you walk away based on a vague picture, you can lose support you still need. Getting it back takes months.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Neptune {{aspectWord}} your Venus. You want to see the best in people and offers, and for months you see them as you wish they were. You feel romantic and generous, and bringing up money or schedules seems like it would ruin the mood. That can lead to spending more than you meant, or to ignoring how someone treats you. The disappointment comes later, when the facts show up. Ask about cost and terms before you spend, and watch how someone treats you for several weeks before you commit to them.

You could change your look, start taking care of your body in a new way, or introduce yourself differently to new people. rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the North Node {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. You are learning to tell people what you want and what you will not do, after years of hiding it because someone once called you too much. You could turn down a role you have always accepted, or go after something you were taught to be ashamed of wanting. Saying it can bring up embarrassment and fear about how people will react. People who have gotten used to you going along with everything may push back. If you hide what you want again, it comes out later as resentment and sharp remarks you did not plan.

Sticking to what you already know feels safer, and it keeps you saying what you have said for years.

Your reactions can be stronger than you expect. Falling back on old coping habits feels safer, and it leaves you handling everything by yourself, the way you always have.

packageRecord.body_you_alternate:

A small disappointment can feel like evidence about the whole week until a meal, walk, conversation, or night of sleep changes the scale again. This is a direct contact, so a new role requiring practice is not happening in the background. It becomes part of the way you handle the situation itself.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the North Node {{aspectWord}} your Neptune. You are drawn toward imaginative work and toward caring for people who are struggling, and neither comes naturally to you yet. You could start painting or writing, take up a spiritual practice, or give time to someone who needs care. This kind of growth is hard to measure, so you can feel unsure you are doing it right. You need more sleep and more time alone. If you call these interests impractical and drop them, you give up the part of your life where you are growing.

You could hand a decision to someone else, end an arrangement that only worked because you managed every detail, or find out how shared money is being handled. Letting go is frightening, because control has kept you safe for a long time. If you hold on tighter, you keep having the same argument about who decides.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Jupiter. For a long period you want more, and the openings that come your way often come from someone with power over you. A bigger role or deal can ask you to give up more control than you notice at first. You could push too hard to grow, sure that more is always better. Taking on too much costs money and independence. Before you take the offer, read the terms and find out who makes the decisions afterward.

Ask what you would give up and who decides when you disagree, before you say yes.

You could get access to money, influential people, or knowledge that helps you build a project or business that lasts. Your judgment about where to put your effort is good. With every option looking promising and nothing pushing back, you could say yes to all of it. Then there is no time left to use what you gained. Say yes to the one that builds on work you do well.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. Anger and desire you have held down for years come up with force, usually around someone who has set the terms of your life for too long. You might refuse a compromise you used to accept without complaint. You could want to punish that person or win outright. Both keep you in the fight longer. Decide which arrangement has to end, and change it over time by asking for what you want and saying no.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. Over this long stretch, you take back control in parts of your life where someone else has been making the decisions. You can do it without rage. You could change how money is handled in a relationship, or end an arrangement that gave another person too much say in your choices. The anger you held down for years shows you where that happened. You are no longer afraid of how strongly you want things. Because you move slowly and do not need to punish anyone, the other person has less to fight, and the change lasts.

They are less afraid of how intense they are, which makes them easier to be around.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Mars. Your drive and your anger are both stronger for months, and you can feel them as tension in your jaw and shoulders. When a person or a rule blocks you, it feels personal. You could push until someone gives in. That force gets hard work done, and it also turns ordinary problems into fights over who is in charge. You can win the argument and still not finish the work. Before you push, figure out what is blocking you.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Mercury. Your thinking is intense and probing for months, and conversations can turn into fights over who gets the last word. You could replay a remark for days, dig for hidden motives, or press a point until the other person goes silent. That focus is useful for research and negotiation. In everyday conversation it makes people defensive. They stop telling you what they meant. Say your point once, then ask what they heard.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Midheaven. Your public role and your standing come under heavy pressure for a long stretch. Who has control over your direction becomes hard to ignore. You could clash with someone who has authority over you. Your place can change when a workplace, a school, or a group you belong to changes how it is run. You might also realize you no longer want the position you worked so hard to reach. Losing standing can feel like losing yourself, so you could fight for every piece of it. That fight can cost you months and goodwill over a role you were already doubting.

You could be trusted with bigger decisions at work, asked to lead a change in your neighborhood or a volunteer group, or given the final say in a family matter. Because it comes without much friction, it is easy to take on more power without deciding what to do with it. If you do not decide, other people will put your influence to work on their own plans.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Moon. For a long stretch, your feelings hit harder than you are used to, especially about home, family, and the people you depend on. A move, a change in the household, or an old family pattern can set you off. When you feel this exposed, you might sleep badly, check where everyone is, or make new rules at home so nothing else changes. That urge to control comes from fear of losing people, and it tends to push them away. When you catch yourself checking up on someone, tell them you are scared instead.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Moon. Over this long period, you can look at your own emotional habits without being scared. The way you react when family plans change, or when someone close lets you down, starts to make sense, and you stop acting on some of those old reactions. You might repair things with a relative or let go of a grudge you have carried for years. Nothing is forcing any of it, so it is easy to put off for another year.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Neptune. A belief or ideal you have relied on for years stops holding up when you look at it closely. You could lose faith in a person or a cause, or notice how many hours go to habits that help you avoid your problems. Losing a belief that comforted you hurts, and the empty feeling makes you want a replacement fast. Anyone who sounds sure of themselves right now can talk you into more than you would normally agree to.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your North Node. You are being pushed hard toward a direction that is new to you and probably uncomfortable. A new role, relationship, or way of working can feel impossible to resist and frightening at the same time, as if going back is no longer an option. For a while you will be bad at parts of it, and being a beginner again can feel like a threat to who you are. Practice the skill this direction needs most every week, even while you are still bad at it.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Pluto {{aspectWord}} your Saturn. For a long time, the structures you count on, like your job or your long-term plans, are under strain. A plan you built carefully could stop working, or someone in authority could demand more than you can give. When you are afraid of failing, you hold on tighter and work harder to keep a broken arrangement running. That effort costs you sleep and wears you out. The arrangement stays broken.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Saturn {{aspectWord}} your Chiron. For many months, an old feeling that you are not good enough runs into responsibilities you cannot put off, and you have to deal with both at once. You could be handling the kind of task you were once told you were bad at, like managing money, taking an exam again, or looking after your health after years of ignoring it. Getting older can bring the old hurt back up. Some days you will be tired in your body and discouraged at the same time. Progress comes from doing the hard task again and again. Every time you finish it, you have one more piece of proof that the old judgment was wrong.

rows.headline: Saturn trine your Descendant
rows.body:
Until {{untilDate}}, Saturn trines your natal Descendant, and something about dealing with other people may feel less complicated than it has. Not effortless. Just clearer. A person follows through. A conversation stays on the subject. You say what you need, and instead of spending twenty minutes defending it, the other person actually hears you.

This is useful for relationships, negotiations, and agreements that have needed more definition. If something has been vague, you may finally be able to name what each person is responsible for. If someone has been inconsistent, their actions may become easier to read. You are not being asked to believe another promise. You are being given a better view of what happens after the promise is made.

If a commitment has been waiting for a clearer shape, give it one. Put it in writing. Name the expectation. Decide what happens next. Saturn is not interested in making something look serious. It is interested in whether the arrangement can actually hold.

sections.body_they:
Until {{untilDate}}, Saturn trines their natal Descendant, and some of the friction around their closest one-on-one relationships may ease enough for them to see what is actually workable.

Someone may become more consistent with them. A stalled conversation may finally move. They may also find it easier to say, plainly, what they expect from a relationship or agreement without immediately backing away from it to keep the peace. The important part is not that everyone suddenly becomes easier. It is that they can see more clearly who is willing to meet them in the responsibility.

They may use this period to define a relationship, formalize an agreement, or change the terms of something that has been too vague for too long. If they tell you they need something to be clearer, take that seriously. They are paying attention to who follows through, what holds up over time, and which connections can carry more weight without asking one person to carry all of it.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Saturn {{aspectWord}} your Jupiter. Your plans to grow run into limits, and the numbers do not match what you hoped for. An opportunity could stall, a budget could tighten, or a commitment you made earlier could ask more of you than you expected. The disappointment can have you swinging between pushing ahead anyway and deciding nothing will work out. A smaller version of the plan, sized to the time and money you have, is the one most likely to get finished.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Saturn {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. For these months, you treat your own wants as important, and your objections turn into limits you keep. You could tell a relative or someone in charge what you will no longer do, or commit to a plan someone once called selfish. You say it without raising your voice or apologizing, so people have less to argue with and start planning around it. You might have to repeat the same no several times before it is accepted. Every favor you stop doing out of guilt gives you back time, and your body feels less tense.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Saturn {{aspectWord}} your South Node. Over these months, old habits and familiar duties feel heavier, and some of them come back to you because you have always handled them. Saying yes is easy, because you know how to do the work and you like being the one people count on. The cost is time and attention you need for what you are trying to grow into. Some of these duties are ending, and taking them back keeps them going longer. Next time, try saying, "I can show you how, but I can't take it on."

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Saturn {{aspectWord}} your Sun. For months, you work hard and get little credit for it. Your energy and confidence run lower, and a boss, parent, teacher, or other authority can be tough on you. Work you are proud of gets criticized or ignored. That hurts, and it makes every setback feel like a verdict on who you are. It is information about where your effort goes. The commitments you keep only for approval are the ones draining you, and this is when you see them clearly.

rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, Saturn {{aspectWord}} your Venus. Month by month, what you want to buy or do starts showing its full price in money, time, or future obligation. An appealing purchase or invitation can look harmless and turn into a long commitment, like a gym contract or a subscription. Saying no can feel unkind, so you could agree to plans you will be paying for long after the fun is over. The charges that repeat every month are the ones most likely to turn into resentment.

rows.headline: An old way of coming across is ending.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Ascendant. For about two months, you go back to old ways of looking and acting, the ones that take no effort. You could wear what you wore years ago, play the part you always played in your family or friend group, or return to an old habit with food or sleep. It feels comfortable at first, then tiring, because it fits who you were. People from your past turn up and treat you the way they did back then. Part of how you used to come across is ending, and it can feel like losing something you knew how to do well.

rows.headline: An old hurt returns, and the old way of coping with it ends.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Chiron. For about two months, an old hurt comes back, and you cope with it the way you learned to long ago. You could find yourself apologizing before anyone complains, avoiding the subject that always stung, or helping everyone else with their pain so you do not have to look at yours. Someone connected to that old hurt can come back into your life, or a familiar situation repeats. Coping the old way tires you more than it used to. The role you built around this hurt is ending. It kept you safe for years, so letting it go can feel like a loss.

rows.headline: An old belief stops working, and it is hard to let go.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Jupiter. Over the next two months or so, you return to the beliefs and habits that have always made you feel lucky or sure of yourself. You could give advice you have given many times before, say yes to more than you can handle because people count on your generosity, or go back to a teacher or a plan you had moved past. It feels good at first. Then it starts to cost you time and money you do not have. A belief you have relied on for years stops making sense to you. Letting it go is hard, because it once got you through a bad time.

rows.headline: The old habit of hiding what you want is ending.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Lilith. For about two months, the wants and the anger you learned to hide come back, and so do the old ways you hid them. You could catch yourself keeping a pleasure secret, going along with something you resent until the anger comes out all at once, or feeling ashamed of what you want the way you did years ago. A person from that earlier time can come back and bring the old shame with them. Keeping all of it to yourself is tiring, and you can see how much of your life it has taken. An old habit of hiding what you want is ending. That is scary at first, because hiding is how you avoided being judged.

rows.headline: An old fight is ending, and you are tired of pushing.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Mars. For about two months, you fight and push the way you always have, and it wears you out faster than it used to. You could get into the same argument with the same person, push your body through a workout or a workday the way you did years ago, or go after a goal by force because force has worked before. Your energy can drop without warning. An old fight or an old goal is ending. Dropping it feels like giving up, even though lately it has mostly worn you down.

rows.headline: Old stories get repeated, and an old way of thinking ends.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Mercury. For a couple of months, you think and talk in the ways you always have. You could repeat stories and opinions you have shared for years, or hear from a sibling or an old classmate you had not heard from in a long time. Talking this way takes no effort, and it leaves you bored. A subject you have known well for years, or an old way of explaining yourself, stops interesting you. Letting it go can leave you unsure what to say for a while.

rows.headline: The role you are known for is ending.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Midheaven. For about two months, the role you are known for is easy to keep playing and tiring to keep up. Someone from an old job, school, or group can ask you back, or you go back to the part you always take in your family or community. People in charge expect the version of you they already know. A title or a role that has defined you for years is ending, or you see that it no longer fits. Losing it can feel like losing your place, even when you were ready to go.

rows.headline: Old family patterns return while something at home ends.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Moon. For about two months, you go back to old ways of feeling at home. You could spend more time with family, take care of everyone the way you did growing up, or want the food and routines you had when you were young. Old moods come back with them, and you can feel like a child again around your parents or siblings. Being in the old role feels safe, and it takes more out of you than you notice. A home arrangement or a family role you have had for years is ending, and it is sad to see it go.

rows.headline: An old dream ends, and old escapes come back.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Neptune. For a couple of months, the ways you have always escaped come back. You could spend long hours on your phone or in front of the TV, daydream about a person from your past, or drop everything to help someone who needs rescuing, the way you used to. These habits soothe you, and they leave you confused and short on sleep. An old dream, or an idea about how your life would turn out, is ending. Admitting it is over hurts, because you have relied on it to get through hard days.

rows.headline: An old power struggle returns, and an old way of control ends.
rows.body: Through {{untilDate}}, the South Node {{aspectWord}} your Pluto. For about two months, you reach for old ways of staying in control. You could take charge of a crisis the way you always do, check up on someone you worry about, or get pulled into a power struggle with a person from your past. You are good at this, and it takes a lot out of you. A relationship where one person has always held the power, or a long fight over money or who decides, is coming to an end. When it ends, you can feel exposed for a while, since being in charge was how you kept from getting hurt.
